While iris recognition would not be enough to immediately ID their members, it would allow for the creation of an informal database of members and, if suspected identities can be found through other means, would facilitate in confirming potential identifications much more effectively than matching facial features.

To produce iris recognition a near-IR image of their iris must be produced. This could potentially be achieved through the use of a high resolution (e.g. 4K) camcorder which features night shot or similar functionality (e.g. full spectrum modified) and fitted with an IR-pass filter. Ideally, the camera used would feature a reasonably powerful optical zoom lens and be set for the fastest shutter rate possible to produce a clean image. A video which at least shows the Antifa member in the same clothes as another video of them committing the crime would provide credibility but the best source would be a video that both shows them committing a crime then zooms in for a close up of their irises. Fortuitously, the majority of masks and sunglasses would be ineffective in protecting against this since they are generally transparent to near-IR.

On the software front, there are a number of open source iris recognition solutions and, since they operate using image data, those capturing the information do not necessarily have to be tech savvy enough to run analysis. An example posting format would be a reasonably compressed video of the entire incident with some high resolution, losslessly compressed frames grabbed directly from the video of their face to give the recognition software the best possible chance.

Not only would this provide better ammunition in securing effective justice upon the criminals (I am a great believer that physical violence against Antifa by those who support free speech is counterproductive in securing both convictions and public support), it would potentially give them pause for thought if they see a camera set up for near-IR recording at their organised riots.
